explainedBy: The narrator introduces Teresa, the manager's employee, in her office.

storyboard.claim: Teresa Lee is the example of the manager's approach.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cut from the bowling metaphor to a real office.
storyboard.staging: Teresa speaks to the viewer from her desk.

explainedBy: Teresa was trained by old bosses to panic and pass problems up.

storyboard.claim: She started out trained in the old, defensive way.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teresa slumped and worried at her desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the setting to her old habits.
storyboard.staging: A worried, slumped Teresa stands for the old habit.

explainedBy: Teresa pulls out one sheet of paper to tell her story.

storyboard.claim: Teresa holds up a single page.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The old habit is now the story she tells.
storyboard.addedInformation: The single page becomes the object of the scene.
storyboard.staging: Teresa holds a single sheet of paper.

explainedBy: A problem is like a fire, and the old rule is to kick it up the chain.

storyboard.claim: A field problem looks like a fire that must be passed up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fire icon beside a frightened Teresa.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sheet becomes the problem she faced.
storyboard.staging: Teresa afraid next to a fire, the problem she faces.

explainedBy: Teresa panics and calls her boss to pass the problem up.

storyboard.claim: Teresa calls her boss in a panic.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the fire to the call.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone is the means of passing it up.
storyboard.staging: Teresa holds a phone and looks afraid as she calls.

explainedBy: The manager neither rescues nor barks orders; he simply says Good.

storyboard.claim: The manager responds calmly with one word.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager, calm, holding his one page.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From her panic to his calm reply.
storyboard.staging: The manager calmly holds the page and speaks.

explainedBy: After the manager's reply, a long silence falls between the two.

storyboard.claim: The silence between them is the pressure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager and Teresa facing each other in silence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the word to the silence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two people in a visible silence.
storyboard.staging: Manager and Teresa side by side, neither speaking.

explainedBy: The silence is a deliberate technique that makes the manager refuse to take the problem back.

storyboard.claim: The silence is an engineered technique.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same two people in the same silence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same scene, the silence is named as a technique.
storyboard.staging: The same silent pair, now labelled as technique.

explainedBy: The manager hands the problem back to Teresa.

storyboard.claim: The manager returns the problem to her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager reaching the page toward Teresa.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From silence to the act of handing it back.
storyboard.addedInformation: The page is the object handed back.
storyboard.staging: Manager reaches the page toward Teresa.

explainedBy: Teresa stammers and waits for instructions she does not get.

storyboard.claim: Teresa stammers, unsure how to solve it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the handing back to her reaction.
storyboard.staging: Teresa afraid facing the manager who waits.

explainedBy: The manager does not budge and makes Teresa state the problem herself.

storyboard.claim: The manager insists she define the problem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager firm, Teresa in front of him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From her stammer to his firmness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the manager holding his ground.
storyboard.staging: Manager calm and firm facing Teresa.

explainedBy: The goal written on one page is the foundation: clarity beats volume.

storyboard.claim: The goal on one page is the foundation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target icon for the one-page goal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the person to the goal itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: The target is the one-page goal.

explainedBy: A goal you cannot read in one minute is too long.

storyboard.claim: A goal must be readable in one minute.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock for the one-minute limit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the target to the time limit.
storyboard.addedInformation: The clock marks the one-minute rule.

callout.text: The OKR document runs to fifty pages

explainedBy: Corporate goal documents are massive, dense binders.

storyboard.claim: Corporate goal documents are huge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A book icon for a long document.
storyboard.onScreenText: The OKR document runs to fifty pages
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the one page to the massive document.
storyboard.addedInformation: The book icon shows the bulk.

explainedBy: The long documents are buried and nobody reads them.

storyboard.claim: Nobody reads these long goal documents.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worker blank and slumped holding notes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the document to the reader.

explainedBy: The Pareto principle is the reason for one page.

storyboard.claim: The one page follows the Pareto principle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Teresa pointing at her one sheet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the documents to the principle.
storyboard.staging: Teresa points to the single sheet.

explainedBy: Eighty percent of the results come from twenty percent of the work.

storyboard.claim: A small share of effort gives most results.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Spectrum from 20 percent effort to 80 percent results.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the principle to its numbers.

explainedBy: You write only three to five key areas, not every task.

storyboard.claim: Only three to five key areas go on the page.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the ratio to the sheet's contents.

explainedBy: A goal longer than a paragraph is hiding behind complexity, which is rejected.

storyboard.claim: A long goal is rejected.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The manager pointing at the sheet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the list to the rejected length.

explainedBy: The young employee struggles to picture the one-page goal for a complex project.

storyboard.claim: The employee struggles with one-page goals.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young employee worried and slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the rule to the doubt.

explainedBy: A massive software rollout is the example of a huge project.

storyboard.claim: A software rollout is a huge project.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Paul with a laptop at a workstation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the doubt to a concrete example.
storyboard.staging: Paul holds a laptop at a workstation.

explainedBy: A huge project has many parts: dependencies, compliance and moving parts.

storyboard.claim: A huge project has many parts.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Paul's example to its parts.

explainedBy: It is impossible to fit that project into a single paragraph.

storyboard.claim: A complex project cannot fit one paragraph.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the parts to the impossibility.

explainedBy: The goal is not the to-do list; that is the rejected reading.

storyboard.claim: The goal is not the to-do list.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Paul's objection to the correction.

explainedBy: The goal is the final outcome and performance standard.

storyboard.claim: The goal is the final outcome.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the rejected to-do to the outcome.

explainedBy: Without a single goal, nobody knows what done looks like.

storyboard.claim: Nobody knows what done looks like.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the outcome to the unknown.

explainedBy: The bowling execution has many parts: the swing, the wrist, the release.

storyboard.claim: The execution is many small movements.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the doubt to the execution parts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Breaks the bowling move into parts.

explainedBy: The goal is the definition of victory: knocking down the pins.

storyboard.claim: The goal is the win, not the technique.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the parts to the goal.

explainedBy: Teresa states what her one-page goal would be.

storyboard.claim: Teresa's example goal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the bowling goal to Teresa's goal.
storyboard.staging: Teresa holds her sheet and talks.

explainedBy: The goal names the downtime to reduce.

storyboard.claim: The goal is to cut downtime by 15 percent.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same scene: the goal is stated.
storyboard.staging: Teresa points at the goal on her sheet.

explainedBy: The goal adds the constraint of no more overtime cost.

storyboard.claim: The goal has a cost limit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same scene: the constraint is added.
storyboard.staging: Teresa holds her sheet and points.

explainedBy: She checks her one page every morning before meetings.

storyboard.claim: She reviews the page every morning.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same scene: the habit is added.

callout.text: Teresa reads the page every morning

explainedBy: Because the page is short, she actually reads it.

storyboard.claim: The short page gets read.
storyboard.onScreenText: Teresa reads the page every morning
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same scene: the behavior is named.

explainedBy: A fifty-page manual is rejected: the brain will not review it.

storyboard.claim: A long manual is rejected.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the page to the rejected manual.

callout.text: There is no hiding behind jargon

explainedBy: Clarity is the opposite of hiding behind corporate jargon.

storyboard.claim: Clarity is not jargon.
storyboard.onScreenText: There is no hiding behind jargon
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the manual to jargon.

explainedBy: The narrator asks how the one page is actually written.

storyboard.claim: How is the page written.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager and Teresa side by side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the goal to the question.
storyboard.staging: Manager and Teresa side by side.

explainedBy: One person writing the goal and handing it down is autocratic control.

storyboard.claim: A manager writing goals alone is autocracy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the question to the answer.

explainedBy: Goals are born in a collaborative process between manager and employee.

storyboard.claim: Goals are written together.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Manager and Teresa side by side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From autocracy to collaboration.
storyboard.staging: Manager and Teresa side by side.
